data.narrative:
NextSilicon, a Series B–stage AI & Software company founded by Elad Raz that has raised $200M+, is valued using a composite of 7 same-sector and adjacent-stage private peers alongside stage-progression methodology. The peer set spans Figure AI ($39.0B, Series C), Reflection AI ($25.0B, Series A), Skild AI ($14.0B, Series C), Crusoe Energy ($10.0B, Series C), Together AI ($8.3B, Series A), and two additional comparables, with a median valuation of $10.0B and a range of $3.2B–$39.0B. One public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR) provides additional sector context.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the $200M total raised as a proxy base, yielding $380M. Peer-median directly derives the $10.0B figure from the seven-company cohort in the same sector at the same or adjacent stage.

Triangulation across these two methods produces a low bound of $323M, a median of $5.2B, and a high bound of $11.5B. The substantial spread reflects material dispersion in peer valuations and the difference between stage-progression and market comparables. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the peer set given wide stage variation (Series A to Series C) and the appropriateness of the 1.9x multiplier for this specific capital stack and market environment. The median of $5.2B balances these approaches but should be treated as directional absent additional revenue or growth metrics.
